title: Software License Compliance & Audit-Defense (Effective License Position)
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (compliance: entitlement-vs-deployment reconciliation, ELP build, audit preparation; high risk/financial exposure).
hook: Know your true license position before a vendor auditor does
problem: A software audit letter shouldn't trigger a fire drill. Without an Effective License Position (ELP) — entitlements reconciled against actual deployment — you can't prove compliance, and shortfalls become expensive settlements. This solution builds a defensible ELP and audit-readiness posture: reconcile what you own against what you run, close gaps before they're found, and walk into any audit with the numbers already in hand.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — what an Effective License Position is, the entitlement ↔ deployment reconciliation model, common compliance gaps, and the audit-defense posture.

Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (entitlement system of record, deployment/usage discovery, product use rights, a reconciliation method, owner sign-off) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.

Implementation Guide — exact, ordered steps: gather entitlements and proofs of purchase, collect deployment/usage, normalize and reconcile to an ELP, identify and close gaps, assemble the audit package, then pilot, validate, and expand to more publishers.
5 PowerShell scripts — deployment discovery, entitlement-vs-deployment reconciliation validation, an ELP and gap report, safe remediation of over-deployment, and a reconciliation-scope group builder.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates, plus field-proven Best Practices for the assign-once, repeat-everywhere model.
short: Build a defensible Effective License Position and audit-readiness posture — reconcile entitlements against deployment, close gaps before they're found, and walk into any audit with the numbers in hand. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
short_plain: Build a defensible Effective License Position and audit-readiness posture — reconcile entitlements against deployment, close gaps before they're found, and be ready for any audit.
